papers.title: Translational Toxicology of N-Isopropylbutylone: Integrated In Vivo and In Silico Assessment of a New Synthetic Cathinone.
papers.abstract: The novel psychoactive substance (NPS) phenomenon represents a major global problem. Despite the methodical inclusion of new analogues in lists of controlled drugs, new compounds continue to circulate, frequently resulting in fatal intoxications. The emergence of N-isopropyl butylone (NiPB) in 2024, found as an adulterant in methamphetamine-based products, underscores the rapidly evolving landscape of NPSs. Despite its structural similarity to potent monoamine transporter inhibitors, specific pharmacological data and information on its effects in consumers are currently lacking. This study aim
papers.summary: This study characterizes N-isopropylbutylone (NiPB), a new synthetic cathinone that appeared in 2024 as an adulterant in methamphetamine products, using combined in vivo and computational (in silico) approaches. The authors assess its toxicological and pharmacological profile to inform risk assessment for this emerging novel psychoactive substance. The work highlights the rapid evolution of NPSs and the need for translational toxicology data on newly circulating compounds.

papers.title: Predicting Rates of Cognitive Decline in Older Adults with Brain- and Cardiac-Imputed Transcripts.
papers.abstract: Severe cognitive decline due to dementia is an important clinical indicator signaling neurodegeneration. Predicting cognitive decline rates can be useful in establishing prognosis and modifying treatment regimens. The rate of decline is highly variable across patients with dementia and may be determined by an interplay of many factors. This variability poses challenges to existing tools for predicting disease progression. Changes in heart and brain tissue have been associated with cognitive decline, yet tissue-specific molecular data are difficult to obtain. In this study, we sought to estimat
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint uses computational imputation to estimate tissue-specific gene expression in brain and heart from more accessible data, then tests whether these imputed transcriptomic profiles can predict the rate of cognitive decline in older adults. The approach aims to overcome the difficulty of obtaining brain and cardiac tissue directly, offering a potential route to molecularly informed prognosis in dementia.

papers.title: PCA-mapping and machine learning identify multiple chemotypes with antiplasmodial, β-haematin and haemozoin formation inhibition activity.
papers.abstract: Inhibiting the formation of haemozoin remains a robust, non-genomic target for antiplasmodial drug discovery. While current efforts focus on multistage active compounds that are not pure haemozoin formation inhibitors, this class offers advantages including selectivity for Plasmodium and is associated with lowered resistance risks. With a view to developing cost-effective tools to streamline the discovery process, we developed a high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS) workflow integrating both ligand- and structure-based techniques. Here, we employed a principal component analysis (PCA) enric
papers.summary: The authors developed a high-throughput virtual screening workflow combining ligand-based and structure-based methods, including PCA-based mapping and machine learning, to identify compounds that inhibit haemozoin formation in Plasmodium parasites. This approach uncovered multiple chemotypes with antiplasmodial, β-haematin inhibition, and haemozoin formation inhibition activity, offering a cost-effective strategy for antimalarial drug discovery targeting a non-genomic pathway.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Potential of the Edible Seaweed Pterocladiella capillacea: Bioactivity Coupled LC-MS/MS, Metabolomics Annotation, Validation, and Network Pharmacology.
papers.abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder with a global impact, highlighting an urgent need for effective dietary therapeutic agents for the development of brain-healthy functional foods and medicines. This study focuses on the edible red alga Pterocladiella capillacea from Zhanjiang, China, investigating its anti-neuronal injury activity, active principles, and underlying mechanisms. Methods: Based on antioxidant and neuroprotection evaluations and column fractioning, bioactivity-coupled liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (Bio-LC-MS/MS) was emplo
papers.summary: This study investigates the edible red seaweed Pterocladiella capillacea for neuroprotective compounds relevant to Alzheimer's disease. Using bioactivity-guided fractionation coupled with LC-MS/MS and metabolomics annotation, the authors identify active constituents and use network pharmacology to predict their mechanisms of action against neuronal injury. The work supports the seaweed's potential as a source of brain-healthy functional food ingredients.

papers.title: The Glyco-Code Molecular Template Instructively Guides Skeletal and Neural Development, Tissue Regeneration and Dynamic Repair Responses Following Trauma and Disease.
papers.abstract: Glycosaminoglycans encode instructional information that cells can decipher to regulate tissue development, repair responses, regeneration and recovery of tissue function following trauma or disease. This information has been termed the glyco-code and is a road map for tissue development and repair. This review shows that a clearer understanding of the glyco-code will support improved strategies in repair biology, particularly in skeletal and neural repair, regeneration, and therapeutic biomaterial design. Emerging therapeutic approaches for peripheral nerve repair increasingly combine multimo
papers.summary: This review argues that glycosaminoglycans carry instructional 'glyco-code' information that cells decode to direct tissue development, repair, and regeneration. The authors synthesize evidence that understanding this code could improve strategies for skeletal and neural repair, including the design of therapeutic biomaterials and combined approaches for peripheral nerve repair.

papers.title: In Vitro Anticancer Activity and Integrated Multi-Target Computational Analysis of Ylang-Ylang Essential Oil Against Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Ylang-ylang essential oil (YEO), obtained from Cananga odorata, contains chemically diverse constituents with potential anticancer activity that warrants further investigation. This study investigated the anti-breast-cancer potential of YEO through an integrated experimental and computational approach. The essential oil was chemically characterized by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, and its in vitro cytotoxic activity was evaluated against ER-positive MCF-7 and triple-negative MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-436 breast-cancer cell lines using the MTT assay. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were
papers.summary: This study characterizes the chemical composition of ylang-ylang essential oil and tests its cytotoxic effects on ER-positive and triple-negative breast cancer cell lines, finding dose-dependent anticancer activity with selectivity relative to normal peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The authors complement the in vitro work with computational multi-target analysis to propose molecular mechanisms and protein targets underlying the observed effects.

papers.title: A Drug-Referenced Machine-Learning Framework for Prioritizing Korean Herbal Formulations in Hypertension Using Linear SVM and Graph Convolutional Networks.
papers.abstract: Hypertension is regulated by interacting molecular systems, providing a rationale for network-based screening of multicomponent therapeutic candidates. Grounded in the conceptual framework of network pharmacology, we developed a hypertension-focused computational framework to prioritize insurance-covered Korean herbal formulations using protein-protein interaction networks derived from marketed antihypertensive and comparator drugs. Thirty reference-drug graphs (15 antihypertensive and 15 comparator drugs) were evaluated using four molecular classifiers under repeated group-aware nested cross-
papers.summary: The authors built a computational pipeline that uses protein-protein interaction networks from known antihypertensive drugs to rank Korean herbal formulations for hypertension, combining linear SVM and graph convolutional network classifiers. Thirty reference-drug graphs (15 antihypertensives, 15 comparators) were evaluated under repeated group-aware nested cross-validation to prioritize insurance-covered herbal candidates. The work is a network-pharmacology screening framework rather than a clinical validation.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Novel Therapeutic Opportunities in Precision Oncology.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping molecular oncology by making complex biological data tractable and by extending the reach of precision drug discovery. Its emerging value is particularly evident at the interface of immunoengineering and targeted therapy, where computational models can help prioritize tumor-selective antigens, predict neoantigen immunogenicity, optimize engineered receptors, support antibody and antibody-drug conjugate design, guide small-molecule discovery, refine genome-editing strategies, and anticipate treatment response. Across these applications, the central prom
papers.summary: This review argues that AI is becoming a practical catalyst across precision oncology, particularly where immunoengineering meets targeted therapy. It surveys computational approaches for prioritizing tumor-selective antigens, predicting neoantigen immunogenicity, optimizing engineered receptors, designing antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates, guiding small-molecule discovery, refining genome editing, and anticipating treatment response. The emphasis is on how AI makes complex biological data tractable and extends the reach of precision drug discovery.

papers.title: qcGEM: A Graph-Based Molecular Representation With Quantum Chemistry Awareness.
papers.abstract: The advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped drug discovery. AI-based models typically rely on molecular representations for prediction. However, the absence of physically grounded information in mainstream molecular representations not only limits the model performance in practical applications but also hinders mechanistic understanding and exploitation by humans. To overcome this issue, we introduce qcGEM, a quantum-chemistry-aware graph-based embedding of molecules that incorporates physical priors into molecular representation learning. Through a specially designed model ar
papers.summary: qcGEM is a new graph-based molecular representation that incorporates quantum chemistry information (physical priors) into the learned embedding, aiming to overcome the lack of physically grounded information in mainstream molecular representations. The authors argue this improves both predictive performance in drug discovery tasks and mechanistic interpretability compared to conventional representations.

papers.title: AI-integrated iPSC multi-omics: advancing phenotype discovery and drug target identification in rare diseases.
papers.abstract: Rare diseases represent a major unmet medical need, yet the development of therapeutics for these diseases is limited by small patient cohorts, fragmented data, and uncertain disease mechanisms. Recent advances that combine patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models with multi-omics profiling and artificial intelligence offer a robust approach for phenotype definition and drug target identification that requires only minimal patient material. By integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data, machine learning can produce disease-relevant molecular signatures, iden
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models with multi-omics profiling and artificial intelligence can overcome the challenges of rare disease research, such as small patient cohorts and fragmented data. By integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data, machine learning can generate disease-relevant molecular signatures and identify drug targets using minimal patient material.

papers.title: Advancing Pregnancy and Pediatric Science through the NIH Transporter Elucidation Network.
papers.abstract: Human gestation is characterized by dynamic changes in maternal physiology and maturation of tissue functions before and after birth. The fetus and neonate are highly dependent upon transfer of maternal nutrients via the placenta and lactating mammary gland, which frequently involve selective membrane transporter proteins. At the same time, developmental changes in fetal and infant transport mechanisms critical for regulating absorption at the intestinal and blood-brain barriers are occurring. Coordinate regulation of cellular entry and efflux of nutrients, supplements, and xenobiotics, includ
papers.summary: This paper describes the NIH Transporter Elucidation Network, a new initiative aimed at understanding how membrane transporter proteins function during pregnancy and early childhood development. It highlights how dynamic changes in maternal physiology and infant tissue maturation affect the selective transfer of nutrients, supplements, and drugs across the placenta, mammary gland, intestine, and blood-brain barrier. The network's goal is to advance research on transporter biology to improve drug safety and nutrient delivery for pregnant women and children.

papers.title: CLEAN Database: providing enzyme function coverage for over 55 million sequences.
papers.abstract: Enzyme function annotation is critical for decoding biological systems and enabling rational enzyme design. However, experimentally characterized enzyme functions remain available for only a small fraction of known protein sequences, resulting in a widening gap between rapidly expanding sequence space and reliable functional assignments. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have accelerated enzyme function annotation by facilitating accurate and high-throughput prediction from protein sequences. Here, we present CLEAN Database (CLEAN DB), a comprehensive resource encompassing >55 mi
papers.summary: CLEAN DB is a new database providing enzyme function annotations for over 55 million protein sequences, using AI-based prediction to bridge the gap between the vast number of known sequences and the small fraction with experimentally characterized functions. It serves as a comprehensive resource for enzyme function annotation, supporting both biological research and rational enzyme design.

papers.title: From artificial intelligence promise to translational practice in drug discovery: Reproducibility, validation and evidence-based implementation.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can support drug discovery, but benchmark performance alone does not establish experimental, operational or clinical benefit. This keynote review distinguishes predictive generalization, experimental confirmation, workflow utility and clinical outcomes, separating demonstrated failures from missing validation. We critically examine quantitative case studies of benchmark bias, prospective hit finding and clinical development, alongside data quality, reproducibility, uncertainty and governance. Practical recommendations link each intended use to appropriate comparato
papers.summary: This keynote review argues that strong AI benchmark performance in drug discovery does not guarantee experimental, operational, or clinical benefit, and it separates demonstrated failures from cases where validation is simply missing. Through quantitative case studies on benchmark bias, prospective hit finding, and clinical development, it examines data quality, reproducibility, uncertainty, and governance, and offers practical recommendations tying each intended use to appropriate comparators and validation standards.

papers.title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: An Overarching Review.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across neuro-oncology domains to analyze complex, high-dimensional, multimodal data. Despite major advances in the biological understanding and classification of CNS tumors, clinical outcomes for many of them remain poor, reflecting intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity and limitations of conventional reductionist approaches. AI offers a paradigm shift to capture this heterogeneity and provide quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights. This article describes a joint effort across the Response Assessment
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across neuro-oncology to analyze complex, multimodal data from CNS tumors. The authors argue that AI offers a paradigm shift beyond reductionist approaches by capturing intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity and providing quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights. The paper is a joint effort across response assessment efforts, likely aimed at standardizing AI use in brain tumor research and clinical care.

papers.title: Integrated Experimental and Computational Investigation of Fluorinated Benzoylthiourea Derivatives: Structural Characterization, Hirshfeld Surface Analysis, Antioxidant Activity, and MAO-B Inhibitory Potential for Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Three novel fluorinated benzoylthiourea derivatives, namely FBTU1-FBTU3, were successfully synthesized in 79-86% yields and fully characterized using spectroscopic techniques including FT-IR, 1H, 13C and 19F NMR, UV-Vis spectroscopy, elemental analysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD). All three compounds crystallize in the monoclinic system (P21/c for FBTU1 and FBTU3; P21/n for FBTU2) with Z = 4. The crystallographic analysis revealed well-defined molecular geometries stabilized by intramolecular and intermolecular interactions. Hirshfeld surface and energy framework analyses ind
papers.summary: Three new fluorinated benzoylthiourea compounds were synthesized and structurally characterized by spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography, with Hirshfeld surface analysis mapping their intermolecular interactions. The compounds were also evaluated for antioxidant activity and MAO-B inhibition, a target relevant to Parkinson's disease, though the abstract does not report the actual activity results.

papers.title: Comparative anthelmintic activity of artemisinin, dihydroartemisinin, and artesunate against sheep gastrointestinal nematodes: in vitro evaluation and exploratory β-tubulin molecular modeling.
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal nematode infections are an important constraint on small-ruminant production, and increasing anthelmintic resistance has intensified the search for alternative therapeutic compounds. Artemisinin and its derivatives have demonstrated activity against several helminth species, although comparative information regarding their effects on gastrointestinal nematodes remains limited. This study compared the in vitro anthelmintic activity of artemisinin (ART), dihydroartemisinin (DHA), and artesunate (ARTE) and explored β-tubulin as a candidate molecular target using complementary com
papers.summary: This study compared the in vitro anthelmintic activity of artemisinin and two derivatives (dihydroartemisinin and artesunate) against sheep gastrointestinal nematodes, finding differences in potency among the compounds. The authors also used molecular modeling to explore β-tubulin as a possible drug target, suggesting a mechanistic hypothesis for the observed activity. The work supports further investigation of artemisinin derivatives as alternatives amid rising anthelmintic resistance.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian regulators for prioritization of drug repurposing candidates.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by complex molecular mechanisms. Growing evidence indicates that circadian rhythm disruption contributes to disease progression and interacts with pathogenic pathways. Although multi-omics resources, compound perturbation profiles, and pharmacological bioactivity data are increasingly available, their integrative use for drug repurposing prioritization in AD, particularly with explicit consideration of circadian rhythm, remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to prioritize drug repurposing candida
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian rhythm regulators to prioritize drug repurposing candidates. By combining compound perturbation profiles and pharmacological bioactivity data, the authors identify existing drugs whose effects align with AD-relevant and circadian-linked pathways. The work highlights circadian biology as an underused axis for AD therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists.
papers.abstract: Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level "Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy." We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.
papers.summary: This perspective reviews how large language model-driven AI agents are moving drug discovery beyond task-specific tools toward autonomous 'virtual scientists.' The authors propose a 6-level 'Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy' to assess system maturity and argue for new evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability, while outlining adoption barriers and positioning agents as scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning framework for peptide lead optimization in ultralarge design spaces.
papers.abstract: In modern peptide drug discovery, the incorporation of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) has become a powerful strategy to improve potency and key developability properties, including stability, solubility, and oral bioavailability. This shift has expanded peptide chemical diversity and design spaces well beyond natural residues, creating fundamental challenges for predictive methods (e.g., quantitative structure-activity relationship modeling) used in lead optimization: limited transferability from natural residues to novel ncAAs, limited interpretability, and poor scalability to ultralarge pe
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable machine learning framework for optimizing peptide leads that incorporate noncanonical amino acids, addressing the poor transferability and scalability of traditional QSAR models in ultralarge chemical design spaces. The approach aims to make predictions more interpretable while handling the expanded chemical diversity beyond natural residues.

papers.title: Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand-bound protein complexes and ranking them by affinity are central problems in drug discovery. While deep-learning co-folding methods can help address these challenges, their evaluation has been hampered by the difficulties in assessing independence from training data and insufficiently large test sets. Here, we test the ability of co-folding methods to predict the structures of 551 ligands, 489 of which are of sufficient quality for evaluation, bound to the SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 macrodomain (Mac1) that were determined after the training cutoff dates. AlphaFold3 (AF3), Bo
papers.summary: This study prospectively tested deep-learning co-folding methods on 551 newly determined Mac1-ligand complexes, using structures solved after model training cutoffs to ensure fair evaluation. AlphaFold3 and related methods were assessed for both structure prediction and affinity ranking across three virtual screens. The work provides a large, unbiased benchmark for co-folding performance in a realistic drug-discovery setting.

papers.title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of AKT1 and structure-based drug design by buckwheat derived compounds.
papers.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Sheikh et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. AKT1 is a serine-threonine protein-kinase involved in tumour cell proliferation, survival, metabolism, and therapeutic resistance via activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. However, the comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of AKT1 and systematics identifications of natural AKT1 inhibitors remains limited. T
papers.summary: This study performs a pan-cancer integrative analysis of AKT1, a kinase central to the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, characterizing its expression and alterations across tumor types. The authors then use structure-based drug design to identify buckwheat-derived natural compounds as potential AKT1 inhibitors. The work combines cancer genomics with computational docking to nominate plant-derived candidates for AKT1-targeted therapy.

papers.title: Transforming the Landscape of Drug Innovation in AI Era: AlphaFold 3 and Beyond.
papers.abstract: The traditional drug discovery and development (DDD) pipeline has long been characterized by inefficiency and high costs. The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI), especially AI-based toolkits for protein structure and interaction prediction, exemplified by AlphaFold 3 (AF3), promises to reshape the landscape of drug innovation. AF3 advances structural biology by predicting protein structures and their interactions with a range of biomolecules, including nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and ions, potentially changing the conventional DDD paradigm, although prediction accuracy
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI-based protein structure and interaction prediction tools, especially AlphaFold 3, are reshaping the traditional drug discovery and development pipeline. AF3 extends beyond protein structure prediction to modeling interactions with nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and ions, potentially changing conventional drug discovery paradigms, though prediction accuracy remains a limitation.

papers.title: Machine learning-based brightfield detection of anti-fibrotic effects in a 3D retinal fibrosis model.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spheroid and microtissue models are increasingly used in phenotypic drug discovery, yet their scalability for high-throughput screening often remains limited, constrained by the cost and complexity of conventional imaging-based readouts. Here, we present a morphology-based screening approach using low-resolution brightfield images of human retinal pigment epithelium microtissues (hRPE-MTs) to identify fibrotic and non-fibrotic phenotypes. The results of this study demonstrate that extracting geometric, intensity, and texture features from segmented spheroids enables quan
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning approach that uses low-resolution brightfield images of 3D human retinal pigment epithelium microtissues to distinguish fibrotic from non-fibrotic phenotypes. By extracting geometric, intensity, and texture features from segmented spheroids, the method enables label-free, cost-effective screening for anti-fibrotic drug effects without conventional imaging readouts. This addresses a key scalability bottleneck in high-throughput phenotypic drug discovery using 3D models.

papers.title: Beyond global drug-likeness: The FamDLike framework as a target family-specific drug-likeness score.
papers.abstract: Drug-likeness is a central metric which is used to evaluate the physicochemical profile of small molecules either as a filter for virtual screening or, more recently, as a reward function in generative design tasks. Established scores such as QED are widely adopted for these purposes, although the ligands of different therapeutic target families occupy different regions of physicochemical space. Applying a single global drug-likeness criterion can therefore systematically reward some target classes while penalising others, narrowing the chemical space considered druglike in a way that may not
papers.summary: The paper introduces FamDLike, a drug-likeness scoring framework that is specific to therapeutic target families rather than using a single global criterion like QED. Because ligands for different target classes occupy distinct physicochemical regions, global scores can systematically bias virtual screening and generative design toward certain target families. FamDLike aims to correct this by tailoring drug-likeness evaluation to the target family of interest.

papers.title: TechBio 3.0 closes the drug discovery loop with multimodal AI and generative chemistry.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed molecular prediction and design, yet these advances remain only partially integrated with experimental discovery. We define TechBio 3.0 as an emerging paradigm for closed-loop drug discovery that connects multimodal molecular representations, generative chemistry, and automated experimentation. We examine its early preclinical and clinical evidence, identify remaining technical and translational barriers, and argue that this convergence is beginning to define biotechnology's next era.
papers.summary: This perspective defines 'TechBio 3.0' as an emerging closed-loop drug discovery paradigm that integrates multimodal molecular representations, generative chemistry, and automated experimentation. The authors review early preclinical and clinical evidence for this convergence, identify remaining technical and translational barriers, and argue it is beginning to define biotechnology's next era.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the fungus-specific antifungal protein NFAP2 as a guide for structure-based drug repurposing against Candida albicans. By targeting NFAP2-binding intracellular fungal proteins such as glutamate decarboxylase and mitochondrial ATP synthase, the authors identify existing compounds that could be repurposed as antifungals. The work offers a strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging drugs with known safety profiles.

papers.title: Fragment OptimizationSimple SMILES String Manipulation Strategies to Optimize a Hit or Fragment.
papers.abstract: AI/ML-based tools for generative and predictive modeling have become important contributors to small molecule drug discovery, enabling virtual compound design and ADME profiling prior to synthesis. Alongside these methods, simpler nonlearned strategies based on direct SMILES manipulation remain useful, particularly for low data targets. Herein is described a method for fragment optimization in which characters of a SMILES string are systematically replaced with alternative SMILES patterns to generate atom-type swaps, ring expansion/contraction, cyclization, ring opening, and fragment grafts. T
papers.summary: The paper describes a simple, non-machine-learning approach to fragment optimization that works by systematically replacing characters in a SMILES string with alternative SMILES patterns. This generates diverse structural modifications such as atom-type swaps, ring expansion or contraction, cyclization, ring opening, and fragment grafting. The method is positioned as a useful complement to AI/ML generative tools, especially for targets with limited data.

papers.title: Design and Synthesis of New Thiazole Derivatives for Alzheimer's Disease Therapy as a Potential Cholinesterase Inhibitor; Toxicity Prediction and Molecular Docking Studies and Biological Evaluation.
papers.abstract: In this study, thiazole derivatives 13-23 were synthesized as novel cholinesterase inhibitors. Their structures were elucidated using 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and elemental analysis techniques. The binding positions and efficiencies of the designed compounds on the enzyme were investigated through molecular docking studies, and the properties of ADMET were examined using computational methods. Cytotoxicity analyses of the synthesized compounds were performed to screen their inhibitory effects on acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) in vitro. It has been determined that these co
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of a series of new thiazole derivatives (compounds 13–23) as potential cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease therapy. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically, evaluated in vitro for AChE and BChE inhibition and cytotoxicity, and assessed computationally via molecular docking and ADMET predictions. The study identifies thiazole scaffolds with promising inhibitory activity and favorable predicted drug-like properties, though the abstract is truncated and specific potency data are not provided.

papers.title: GNPS-assisted identification of bioactive constituents from Scoparia dulcis and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms via network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Scoparia dulcis L. (SD) is an edible medicinal herb traditionally consumed as a cooling beverage in tropical Asia for the management of metabolic and inflammatory disorders; however, its dietary bioactive constituents and anti-inflammatory mechanisms have not yet been fully elucidated. In the present study, the metabolite profile of the aerial parts of SD (ASD) was characterized, and their anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through an integrated approach incorporating LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in v
papers.summary: This study used GNPS molecular networking of LC-HRMS/MS data to profile metabolites from Scoparia dulcis, an edible medicinal herb, then combined network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict anti-inflammatory targets and mechanisms. Experimental validation supported the predicted anti-inflammatory activity, linking specific constituents to inflammatory pathways.

papers.title: Sartans and Bisartans: Expanding Therapeutic Horizons Through Broad Receptor Interactions and Repurposing Potential.
papers.abstract: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), also known as sartans, are a family of highly selective angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonists commonly prescribed to individuals with hypertension, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. Additionally, the discovery and facile synthesis of bisartans, a novel class of ARB antihypertensives, have shown therapeutic promise for cardiovascular diseases. Recent computational and network pharmacology studies have shown a broader receptor interactome, encompassing alpha-adrenergic receptors, and delta- and mu-opioid receptors, highlighting the polypharmaco
papers.summary: This review examines angiotensin receptor blockers (sartans) and the newer bisartan class, highlighting evidence from computational and network pharmacology studies that these drugs interact with a broader set of receptors than previously recognized, including alpha-adrenergic and opioid receptors. This polypharmacology suggests potential for repurposing sartans beyond cardiovascular indications. The paper synthesizes these findings to outline expanded therapeutic horizons.

papers.title: Integrated In silico and In Vitro Evaluation of Piperine Derivatives as Potential Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance mediated by efflux pump activity represents a major challenge in the treatment of infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Efflux pumps such as NorA and MepA reduce intracellular antibiotic accumulation and contribute significantly to decreased antibiotic efficacy. In this study, PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, was evaluated as a potential efflux pump inhibitor using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Computational analysis, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Lipinski r
papers.summary: This study evaluates PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, as a potential efflux pump inhibitor in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) using combined computational and experimental approaches. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were used to predict binding to NorA and MepA efflux pumps, followed by in vitro testing. The work suggests piperine derivatives may help restore antibiotic efficacy against resistant strains.

papers.title: Thymol-based derivatives as anticancer agents: design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Seventeen thymol-based derivatives (TM1-7, TBr1-2, TCl1-4, and TF1-4) were designed and synthesized by esterification with halo- and non-halogenated cinnamoyl molecules employing a key-step coupling reaction. All derivatives were chemically characterized (1H NMR, 13C NMR, HR-MS, and HPLC analysis) and evaluated for their potential anticancer properties. The anti-proliferative effectiveness was assessed using an MTT assay against four cancer cell lines (U87MG, SHSY-5Y, MDA-MB-231, and JIMT1) and human dermal fibroblasts (HDFa) compared to Triton X-100. Among the thymol-based derivatives, TM7 an
papers.summary: The authors designed and synthesized seventeen thymol-based ester derivatives using cinnamoyl and halogenated cinnamoyl groups, then screened them for anticancer activity against four cancer cell lines (U87MG, SHSY-5Y, MDA-MB-231, JIMT1) and normal human dermal fibroblasts. Compound TM7 emerged as the most promising antiproliferative agent in this series, and molecular docking was used to rationalize its binding to a likely target. The work is a standard medicinal-chemistry structure-activity study identifying a lead compound for further optimization.

papers.title: Discovery and biological characterization of 1-[4-(2-difluoromethoxyphenyl)-5-methylthiazol-2-yl]-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)urea (DFMNTU): A novel thiazolyl-urea chemotype targeting yellow fever virus and host casein kinase 2 (CK2).
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a re- emerging mosquito- borne flavivirus that causes severe hemorrhagic fever with high case- fatality rates. Due to vaccine contraindications, incomplete immunization coverage, and the absence of approved specific antivirals, host- directed drug discovery targeting cellular machinery exploited by YFV is a critical therapeutic priority. Here, 1-[4-(2- difluoromethoxyphenyl)- 5- methylthiazol- 2- yl]- 3-(naphthalen- 1- yl)urea (DFMNTU) was synthesized, characterized by NMR, MS, and HPLC, and evaluated for antiviral efficacy against YFV strain 17 D in Vero cells. DFM
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: The authors synthesized and characterized a novel thiazolyl-urea compound, DFMNTU, and showed it inhibits yellow fever virus (strain 17D) in Vero cells while targeting the host kinase CK2, suggesting a host-directed antiviral strategy. This is an early-stage drug-discovery study identifying a new chemotype against a virus with no approved specific treatment.

papers.title: Design-Evolution Synergy Enables New-to-Nature Enzyme Chemistry.
papers.abstract: Directed evolution and machine-learning-assisted evolution have transformed biocatalysis by enabling rapid optimisation of catalytic performance within compatible protein scaffolds. In parallel, advances in deep-learning-driven de novo protein design have expanded accessible protein architectural space, enabling the generation of functional catalysts for increasingly challenging transformations. We herein report a synergistic design-evolution strategy to encode new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination reactions using engineered de novo haemproteins to synthesise chiral piperidin
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports a hybrid strategy that combines deep-learning-driven de novo protein design with directed evolution to create engineered haemoproteins capable of new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination, yielding chiral piperidines. The work shows that design and evolution can be used synergistically rather than sequentially, expanding the accessible catalytic space beyond what either approach achieves alone.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Chronic Rhinosinusitis: From Molecular Profiling to Personalized Clinical Management-A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease imposing a substantial health and economic burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to address CRS complexity in both clinical and research settings. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase for peer-reviewed articles utilizing machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, with a focus on molecular-level or immunologic mechanisms in CRS. Thirty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Our results de
papers.summary: This systematic review examines 31 studies applying machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing to chronic rhinosinusitis, spanning molecular and immunologic profiling through clinical management. It maps how AI is being used to address the disease's heterogeneity, from endotype discovery to personalized treatment decisions. The review provides a structured overview of current methods and applications in this niche clinical domain.

papers.title: Identification of YES1 Inhibitors From Approved Drugs Using a Multimodal Deep Learning Framework.
papers.abstract: While anti-human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) drugs, including trastuzumab improve the prognosis of patients with HER2-positive cancers, acquired resistance by cancer cells remains a significant clinical challenge. We had previously reported that YES1 is overexpressed in trastuzumab-resistant breast and lung cancer cells, and that its inhibition restores trastuzumab sensitivity. However, no approved drug specifically targets YES1. In this study, as a drug repositioning approach aimed at rapid clinical application, we constructed a machine learning model capable of learning the int
papers.summary: The authors built a multimodal deep learning framework to identify approved drugs that inhibit YES1, a kinase implicated in resistance to HER2-targeted therapy like trastuzumab. By screening existing drugs computationally, they aim to enable rapid drug repurposing to restore trastuzumab sensitivity in resistant HER2-positive cancers. The work presents a machine-learning-based repositioning strategy rather than a validated new therapy.

papers.title: In Silico Evaluation via Virtual Screening, ADMET Profiling and Molecular Dynamics Simulations: Synthesis and Biological Activity Analysis of a Novel Antitumor PI3K Inhibitor.
papers.abstract: The PI3K plays a crucial role in cancer progression, and the development of PI3K inhibitors has always been a hot research direction in oncology. Through virtual screening and docking, potential lead compounds were identified. ADMET prediction revealed that KTC101 possesses superior pharmacokinetic profile. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that compound KTC101 could stably bind to PI3Kδ, with a binding free energy of -374.627 kJ/mol. Analysis of the metabolism of KTC101 revealed that this compound could undergo diverse phase I metabolic reactions catalyzed by hepatic CYP450 enzymes to
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a novel PI3K inhibitor (KTC101) and evaluated it using computational methods including virtual screening, docking, ADMET prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations. They report that KTC101 has favorable pharmacokinetic properties and binds stably to PI3Kδ with a high binding free energy, and they characterize its phase I metabolism by hepatic CYP450 enzymes. The study is primarily computational with limited experimental validation.

papers.title: Targeting a Leukemia-Relevant Protein-Protein Interface: N-Aryl Anthranilic Acids as Disruptors of the c-Myb-CBP/p300 KIX Interaction.
papers.abstract: The interaction between c-Myb and the CBP/p300 KIX domain is a key transcriptional event in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and represents an attractive target for small-molecule intervention. In this study, we applied an integrated computational-experimental strategy to identify new N-aryl anthranilic acid disruptors of the c-Myb-KIX protein-protein interaction. A scaffold-focused library of 3656 N-aryl anthranilic acid derivatives was filtered, docked to the c-Myb-binding groove of KIX (PDB 2AGH), and the top hits were further evaluated by MD simulations, MM/PBSA, FEL, and ADMET analyses. This
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational and experimental approach to identify N-aryl anthranilic acid derivatives that disrupt the c-Myb–CBP/p300 KIX protein-protein interaction, a transcriptional event relevant to acute myeloid leukemia. A scaffold-focused library of 3656 compounds was filtered, docked to the c-Myb-binding groove of KIX, and top hits were evaluated with MD simulations, MM/PBSA, free energy landscape, and ADMET analyses. The work nominates new small-molecule scaffolds for targeting a leukemia-relevant protein interface.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Cotula cinerea Essential Oil: Integrated Chemical, In Vivo, Histological, and Computational Evaluation.
papers.abstract: The anti-inflammatory activity of Cotula cinerea essential oil (EO) was evaluated using integrated chemical, in vivo, histological, and computational approaches. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) identified trans-thujone (51.86%), santolina triene (10.60%), and sabinene (6.17%) as the most abundant constituents. In benzylthiouracil (BTU)-treated Wistar rats, EO administration reduced the liver and kidney indices from 4.36% to 2.70% and from 0.65% to 0.52%, respectively; red blood cell count increased from 4.90 to 7.17 × 1012/L and hemoglobin from 9.40 to 15.40 g/dL. Aspartate aminot
papers.summary: This study characterizes the essential oil of Cotula cinerea by GC-MS (dominated by trans-thujone) and tests its anti-inflammatory effects in rats with benzylthiouracil-induced hypothyroidism/inflammation. EO treatment reduced liver and kidney indices and improved red blood cell count and hemoglobin, with histological and computational (docking) analyses supporting the findings. The work is a conventional ethnopharmacological evaluation of a single plant extract with modest mechanistic depth.

papers.title: Synthesis and Cytotoxic Activity of 1,3-Selenazole-2-Amine Derivatives With Computational ADMET Profiling.
papers.abstract: A set of newly developed 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives (1-4) was prepared via a modified Hantzsch-type cyclization of appropriately substituted α-bromoacetophenones with selenourea under reflux conditions. The synthesized compounds were tested for cytotoxic activity in HT-29 (colon cancer), MCF-7 (breast cancer), and L929 (mouse fibroblast) cell lines using the MTT assay. The compounds induced weak to moderate cytotoxicity in MCF-7 cells. Among them, compound 4 showed cytotoxic activity with IC50 value of 171.10 µM, while no appreciable activity was observed against HT-29 cells (IC50 > 30
papers.summary: The authors synthesized four new 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives via a modified Hantzsch cyclization and tested their cytotoxicity against colon cancer (HT-29), breast cancer (MCF-7), and normal fibroblast (L929) cell lines. The compounds showed only weak to moderate activity, with the best compound (4) having an IC50 of 171 µM against MCF-7 and no appreciable activity against HT-29. Computational ADMET profiling was also performed, but the overall biological activity is modest.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in pharmacy and pharmaceutical sciences: Research output, trends, and thematic priorities - A descriptive analysis of web of science-indexed publications (2010-2025).
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming pharmacy and pharmaceutical sciences (PPS), yet the evolution, research priorities, and global landscape of AI-related research within this field have not been comprehensively characterized.
papers.journal: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
papers.summary: This study provides a descriptive bibliometric analysis of AI-related research in pharmacy and pharmaceutical sciences, using Web of Science-indexed publications from 2010 to 2025 to map research output, trends, and thematic priorities. It characterizes the evolution and global landscape of AI adoption in the field, identifying key areas of focus and growth. The work offers a high-level overview rather than new methodological or experimental findings.

papers.title: Selective PTP1B inhibition by A-1331852: Uncompetitive kinetics and computational evidence for C-terminal engagement.
papers.abstract: Selective inhibition of protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B), a well-established target in metabolic and oncological signaling pathways, is limited by its 74% active-site identity with the closely related phosphatase TCPTP. Repurposing the clinical-stage Bcl-xL BH3 mimetic A-1331852, we identify it as a potent PTP1B inhibitor demonstrating a selectivity margin of at least 50-fold over TCPTP (IC₅₀ = 4.0 μM vs >200 μM). Kinetic analysis reveals uncompetitive inhibition consistent with recognition of a substrate-induced binding site. Docking and 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations (MD) of fu
papers.summary: The clinical-stage Bcl-xL inhibitor A-1331852 was found to also inhibit PTP1B with at least 50-fold selectivity over the closely related phosphatase TCPTP, showing uncompetitive kinetics that suggest binding to a substrate-induced site rather than the active site. Docking and 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations support engagement of a C-terminal region, offering a potential route to selective PTP1B inhibition despite high active-site homology.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and genome mining strategies for activating cryptic polyketide biosynthetic gene clusters in Streptomyces: an overview.
papers.abstract: Beneficial microbes from soil or marine habitats are promising sources for discovery of new bioactive compounds for medicine and agriculture, largely through biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) that encode the production of complex natural products for drug and antibiotic discovery. However, most BGCs are transcriptionally silent under standard testing conditions and may require a complex, integrated approach for activation. In this review, we revisit previous approaches to activating BGCs, focusing on polyketides. We additionally discuss how integrating genome mining strategies with multi-omics
papers.summary: This review surveys strategies for activating silent polyketide biosynthetic gene clusters in Streptomyces, which are a major source of bioactive natural products but are usually not expressed under standard lab conditions. It emphasizes combining genome mining with multi-omics approaches to identify and turn on these cryptic clusters, aiming to unlock new antibiotics and other drugs.

papers.title: Lab to codes: multimodel advanced AI-driven pipelines to drive antimicrobial peptide design for the post-antibiotic era.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has outpaced the development of new antimicrobial agents, necessitating transformative approaches such as AI-driven in-silico drug discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising alternatives due to their broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and limited susceptibility to resistance. However, the transition from bench to bedside remains constrained by certain challenges, such as instability, potency, and cytotoxicity. Here, well-integrated, multi-model AI-driven pipeline strategies for the mining and discovery of novel AMPs are
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrated multi-model AI pipelines can accelerate the discovery and design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights how AI can help overcome key bottlenecks such as peptide instability, potency, and cytotoxicity, moving AMPs from the lab toward clinical use.

papers.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A co
papers.summary: MolecureAI is an autonomous AI agent platform for closed-loop drug discovery that uses cost-ordered cascade evaluation to enforce chemical correctness via structural invariants. It addresses four gaps: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. The platform aims to accelerate identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas.

papers.title: A review of advances in research on mechanisms inhibiting kidney stone formation from a network pharmacology perspective.
papers.abstract: Nephrolithiasis is a prevalent, highly recurrent urological disorder affecting 1%-15% of the global population, with 5-year recurrence rates reaching up to 50%. While surgical interventions achieve acute stone clearance, they do not resolve underlying metabolic derangements, crystal-induced tubular injury, or chronic inflammatory cascades. Natural products from global ethnomedicinal systems (including Traditional Chinese Medicine, Indian Ayurveda, Persian Unani medicine, European phytotherapy, and African ethnopharmacology) demonstrate potent multi-target anti-urolithic properties. However, de
papers.summary: This review examines how network pharmacology can be used to understand the multi-target mechanisms by which natural products from various ethnomedicinal traditions inhibit kidney stone formation. It argues that these compounds act on multiple pathways simultaneously—addressing metabolic imbalances, crystal-induced tubular injury, and inflammation—which single-target approaches miss. The paper synthesizes research on anti-urolithic natural products and the network-based methods used to dissect their mechanisms.

papers.title: Knowledge graph and machine learning-guided virtual screening prioritizes putative blockers of the PSMD11/Rpn6-EBOV glycoprotein interface.
papers.abstract: Host-directed antiviral discovery requires a traceable route from host-factor identification to testable molecular hypotheses. This study developed such a workflow around a host factor associated with Ebola virus glycoprotein (EBOV GP).
papers.summary: The authors built a workflow that combines a knowledge graph with machine learning to prioritize putative small-molecule blockers of the interaction between the host protein PSMD11/Rpn6 and the Ebola virus glycoprotein. Starting from host-factor identification, they generated testable molecular hypotheses for host-directed antiviral candidates. The approach offers a traceable pipeline from data to prioritized compounds.

papers.title: Commentary: Identification of diagnostic genes for myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury associated with metabolic syndrome through the integration of bioinformatics analysis, molecular docking and experimental validation.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses a study that used bioinformatics integration, molecular docking, and experimental validation to identify diagnostic genes linking myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury with metabolic syndrome. It highlights the study's approach to uncovering shared molecular mechanisms and potential biomarkers, while noting limitations and future directions for validating these findings.

papers.title: Single‑Cell in silico Perturbation Uncovers a Ferroptosis Regulatory Network for Cigarette Smoke‑Induced Skin Aging and Identifies Dapivirine as a Candidate Agent.
papers.abstract: Cigarette smoke exposure induces cutaneous ferroptosis and accelerates skin aging, yet the core regulatory genes and targeted interventions remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key ferroptosis-driving genes underlying smoke-induced skin senescence, clarify their mechanisms, and screen candidate small molecules that reverse smoke-related skin damage.
papers.summary: The authors used single-cell in silico perturbation analysis to identify a ferroptosis regulatory network driving cigarette smoke-induced skin aging, then screened for small molecules that reverse the associated gene expression signature. Dapivirine emerged as a candidate agent capable of counteracting the smoke-related skin damage signature.

papers.title: Integrated counter current separation and omics approaches for discovery of bioactive compounds from medicinal plants.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants provide an important source of structurally varied bioactive metabolites with medicinal potential; however, their effective extraction, characterization, and standardization present considerable analytical challenges. Counter-current separation (CCS) methods, such as centrifugal partition chromatography (CPC) and high-speed counter-current chromatography (HSCCC), represent advanced liquid-liquid chromatographic approaches that minimize irreversible adsorption of samples. A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Sci
papers.summary: This review examines how counter-current separation (CCS) techniques like centrifugal partition chromatography and high-speed counter-current chromatography can be combined with omics approaches to discover bioactive compounds from medicinal plants. CCS methods use liquid-liquid partitioning that avoids irreversible sample adsorption, and integrating them with metabolomics and other omics platforms offers a route to more efficient extraction, characterization, and standardization of plant-derived metabolites.

papers.title: Multimodal profiling uncovers an aging-associated ETS1-MYO1B vascular niche responsive to ipragliflozin.
papers.abstract: Tissue aging involves complex changes in vascular, immune, and stromal compartments that collectively reshape the local tissue ecosystem and may contribute to age-related diseases, including cancer, fibrotic diseases, and cardiovascular disease. However, it remains unclear whether reproducible, cell-specific vascular niche states emerge during aging and whether these states can be therapeutically targeted.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Using multimodal profiling, the authors identify a reproducible aging-associated vascular niche state marked by ETS1-MYO1B expression that emerges across tissues during aging. They show this niche can be therapeutically modulated by ipragliflozin, suggesting a targetable vascular component of tissue aging.

papers.title: Potential Molecular Links Between Benzophenone-3 and Breast Cancer: Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Molecular Modeling, and Gene Expression Validation.
papers.abstract: Benzophenone-3 (BP-3) is a widely used ultraviolet filter with potential carcinogenic concern, but its molecular link with breast cancer remains unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate targets and potential molecular links between BP-3 and breast cancer using toxicological prediction, machine learning, molecular modeling, and gene expression analysis.
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, molecular docking, and gene expression validation to identify candidate molecular targets linking the UV filter benzophenone-3 to breast cancer. It proposes potential target genes and pathways through which BP-3 exposure might contribute to breast carcinogenesis, offering hypotheses for future experimental work.

papers.title: Placental alkaline phosphatase promotes lipid accumulation and fibrosis in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy and represents a potential target for statin repurposing.
papers.abstract: Lumbar spinal stenosis is a prevalent degenerative disorder driven primarily by ligamentum flavum hypertrophy. Emerging evidence links ectopic lipid accumulation to fibrotic remodeling and suggests a potential contribution of immune dysregulation. However, the molecular targets connecting lipid accumulation with ligamentum flavum fibrosis remain incompletely defined. We sought to evaluate the underlying mechanisms of lipid-lowering drug targets in lipid-associated ligamentum flavum fibrosis.
papers.summary: This study identifies placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) as a molecular link between ectopic lipid accumulation and fibrosis in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy, a key driver of lumbar spinal stenosis. The authors propose that statins, by lowering lipids, may counteract PLAP-mediated fibrotic remodeling, suggesting drug repurposing potential. The work combines mechanistic investigation with a therapeutic hypothesis but relies on preclinical evidence.

papers.title: Editorial: Exploring untapped potential: innovations in drug repurposing.
papers.summary: This editorial introduces a special issue on drug repurposing, highlighting innovations that expand the use of existing drugs for new therapeutic indications. It likely surveys emerging computational and experimental strategies, such as network-based approaches, AI, and integrative omics, that accelerate repurposing discovery. The piece frames the untapped potential of repurposing to reduce development costs and timelines.

papers.title: 3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic neurological disorder associated with altered dopaminergic signaling, while long-term dopamine agonist therapy may be limited by augmentation and reduced clinical benefit. This study applied a three-dimensional convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder integrated with long short-term memory molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened through pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, pharmacophore ana
papers.summary: The authors combined a 3D convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder with an LSTM generative model to design novel rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors as potential alternatives for restless legs syndrome. Fourteen unique candidates were generated and filtered through pocket prediction, docking, interaction profiling, and pharmacophore analysis. The work is a computational proof-of-concept; no experimental synthesis or biological validation is reported.

papers.title: Identification of flavonoids from natural products against hyperlipidaemia through computational approaches.
papers.abstract: Over the centuries, hyperlipidaemia has been recognised as a major risk factor contributing to cardiovascular disease (CVD). Current research increasingly explores natural compounds such as flavonoids for their potential lipid-lowering effects. This study evaluated pharmacological potential of flavonoids to identify strong inhibitors for target receptor, Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type (PCSK9). A total of 29 compounds, including one FDA-approved drugs were screened for drug-likeness and ADMET properties, followed by molecular docking and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations using PC
papers.summary: This study computationally screened 29 flavonoids and one FDA-approved drug for drug-likeness and ADMET properties, then used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to identify flavonoids that inhibit PCSK9, a key lipid-regulating receptor. The work nominates candidate natural compounds for lipid-lowering activity, but the findings are purely computational and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study computationally screens phytochemicals from the mangrove plant Rhizophora mucronata as potential inhibitors of proteins implicated in non-small cell lung cancer. Using molecular docking and other in silico analyses, the authors identify candidate compounds with favorable predicted binding to lung cancer-associated targets. The work is purely computational and provides hypotheses for future experimental validation rather than demonstrated anticancer activity.

papers.title: Preclinical identification of an oxadiazole-pyrazole lead targeting prostate cancer through integrated mechanistic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among men, while resistance to androgen deprivation therapy emphasizes the need for new therapeutic strategies. Molecular hybridization of pharmacologically relevant heterocycles offers a rational approach for developing novel anticancer agents.
papers.summary: This preclinical study reports the identification of a novel oxadiazole-pyrazole hybrid compound as a lead candidate for prostate cancer therapy, motivated by the need for alternatives to androgen deprivation therapy. The authors use integrated mechanistic evaluation to characterize the compound's anticancer activity, though the abstract provides limited detail on specific targets or in vivo results.

papers.title: GDA-Pred: Generative AI-Driven Data Augmentation for Improved Prediction of IL-6 and IL-13-Inducing Peptides
papers.abstract: The identification of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-13 (IL-13) inducing peptides is crucial for accelerating drug discovery targeting cancer, immune disorders, and infectious diseases. However, experimental screening methods remain time-consuming and costly. To address these limitations, various machine learning and deep learning models have been developed, yet their performance is still constrained by the limited availability of experimentally validated data. In this study, we propose a generative AI-driven data augmentation (GDA) framework and predictor, GDA-Pred, to improve the predi
papers.summary: The authors present GDA-Pred, a framework that uses generative AI to create synthetic peptide data and thereby augment the limited experimentally validated datasets for IL-6- and IL-13-inducing peptides. This data augmentation improves the performance of machine learning/deep learning predictors for identifying immunomodulatory peptides relevant to cancer, immune disorders, and infectious disease drug discovery. The work addresses the common bottleneck of scarce labeled data in peptide bioactivity prediction.
